proposed_2027_family.rule: every original verdict stands as its own rule gives it (each at z > 2, one-sided 0.0228); the family statement is reported BESIDE them: a test is family-confirmed when Holm's step-down at these thresholds rejects it, ordered by z

multiplicity.shared_games: the 2027 tests read the same games: R5's units are a subset of R4's (every strategic pulled team-game is a pulled one) and both sit inside R2-H2's team-games. On the development seasons the correlation of the tests' MEANS (n_shared / sqrt(nA nB) x the per-unit correlation) was R4 x R5 +0.22 (2025) / +0.08 (2026), R2-H2 x R4 -0.10 / +0.05, R2-H2 x R5 +0.02 / -0.05 (family_2027.json): small, positive where the units nest. Holm holds under any dependence. A pass on shared games is weaker evidence than the same pass on independent games: joint passes are not independent confirmations, and a defect common to R3's pull or R4's labels moves R4 and R5 together.

owner_approval.words: Allow R5 to use the 2027 regular season rather than waiting until January 2029. Freeze its implementation and acceptance criteria now. Account explicitly for dependence and multiple comparisons across R1-R5. Preserve all original registrations and verdicts. Do not modify R5 based on the shared evaluation games.

power: 2027 should hold ~45 strategic pulled team-games (424 in 2016-2024; 57 in 2025): criterion 2's power ~0.91 at the development effect (+1.34, SD 2.68) under its own z > 2, ~0.89 at the 2027 family's strictest Holm step (z 2.128); at the 30-game floor ~0.77 and ~0.73. Criterion 3 fails ~2.3% by chance; the corner secondary as in prereg_r5.json. Power is the chance the test passes IF R5 is better by the stated amount, never the probability that it is.
read_order: R1's read (on/after 2027-01-06) first; then R2-H2's and R4's (both on/after 2028-01-13, either order); then this read, which refuses until R1's and R4's results are committed; prereg_r5.json's 2028 read (on/after 2029-01-16) last, as a REPLICATION on games no 2027 read sees
replication: prereg_r5.json stays byte-identical and its 2028 read stands as a later, independent replication: a 2027 PASS is the primary result, the 2028 read its confirmation, and each verdict is reported as its own rule gives it
secondary: reported, never part of the verdict: the trailing corner's real pulls against R5's expectation, one-sided Poisson P(X >= real) < 0.05 = the post-2021 excess persists on fresh games (the evidence a corner-specific term would need)
